summary: The study describes the deposition of TaNx as a diffusion barrier for Cu-interconnect technology using metal-organic plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (MO PE-ALD). The process uses pentakis(dimethylamino)Ta (PDMA T) as a precursor and hydrogen or nitrogen plasma as reactants. The films exhibit good diffusion barrier properties even at subnanometer thicknesses, with the nanocrystalline microstructure contributing to their effectiveness. The study also compares the performance of MO PE-ALD TaNx with that of chloride-based PE-ALD TaNx and highlights the benefits of using a metal-organic precursor to avoid Cl contamination.
evidence: TaNx diffusion barriers with good barrier properties at subnanometer thickness were deposited by plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PE-ALD) from pentakis(dimethylamino)Ta. Hydrogen and/or nitrogen plasma was used as reactants to produce TaNx thin films with a different nitrogen content. The deposited film has nanocrystalline grains with hydrogen-only plasma, while the amorphous structure was obtained for nitrogen plasma. The diffusion barrier properties of deposited TaN films for Cu interconnects have been studied by thermal stress test based on synchrotron x-ray diffraction. The results indicate that the PE-ALD TaN films are good diffusion barriers even at a small thickness as 0.6 nm. Better diffusion barrier properties were obtained for higher nitrogen content. Based on a diffusion kinetics analysis, the nanocrystalline microstructure of the films was responsible for the better diffusion barrier properties compared to polycrystalline PE-ALD TaN films deposited from TaCl5.
